_comment_unmeasured_residue: src/components, src/pages, src/App.tsx and src/main.tsx carry no mutation measurement. They are not negated in mutate below; they fall outside its include globs (src/lib/** and src/hooks/**), so until this key nothing in this file recorded that the omission was deliberate. It is deliberate, and this is its record. It covers the omitted surface only; the three negated files inside src/lib are a different exclusion with different reasons, documented in _comment_mutate above. The list in _unmeasured_residue_files names every production file the globs never reach, taken at main 414a7eb: 37 .tsx files under src/components and src/pages (50 present, less the 13 co-located .test.tsx suites), plus App.tsx at 81 lines and main.tsx at 60. Two of the named files are refused by this note rather than justified by it. Game.tsx is logic-bearing: 1,290 lines carrying 21 className attributes, with state, refs, 24 effects and the persistence-restore, BFCache and completion-gating wiring filling roughly 880 lines before its render tree opens. Menu.tsx is mixed: 1,245 lines carrying 118 className attributes, with logic regions at lines 49-84 (OfflineModeToggle's service-worker registration and cache wiping), 254-289 (ModeSwitchSection's storage-driven mode switching) and 741-892 (the dialog, Escape, new-puzzle-confirmation and cache-clear handlers). Both belong to extraction follow-up, not under this justification. App.tsx and main.tsx are bootstrap glue whose helpers already live on the measured surface; their only branch sites are the route-prefix checks at App.tsx:37-43 and the offline-registration guard at main.tsx:40-42, named rather than sheltered. The rest is presentation: markup and inline SVG over logic already extracted into src/lib and src/hooks. For contrast, 88 files were on the mutate surface at main 414a7eb (81 per-file shards plus the 7 files the hooks matrix covers), 4 of them .tsx: the src/lib React contexts. The excluded set carries less logic than when MUT-8-6 instrumented it at 3,531 mutants, found 53% of them in the 29 files with no dedicated vitest suite, and estimated that admission would drop the aggregate 15 to 20 points; the extraction campaign has since put 18 new files on the surface, counted at main 414a7eb, the current excluded-set mutant count is deliberately not re-derived here because only a Stryker admission run could produce it, and Game.tsx is now the largest unmeasured file. Two things substitute for measurement, and neither is mutation coverage. First, 13 of the 37 files carry a co-located vitest suite: Board, Controls, Dialog, GameHeader, GlossaryLinkedText, History, Menu, ShareModal, TechniqueBoardSvg, Toast, Custom, Game and Result. Those suites run under the same vitest runner Stryker drives, so they would kill mutants if their files were admitted to scope; the files are not admitted, so today they kill none here. They are assertion evidence, not measured evidence, and the distinction is the point of this campaign. Second, the Playwright suite: 39 spec files and 488 test() calls, of which 29 specs and 440 test() calls form the integration tier covering gameplay, hints, keyboard navigation, notes, persistence, sharing, accessibility, leaderboard, custom entry and mobile viewports. That is real behavioural evidence that the rendered application works. It kills exactly zero mutants. It runs under Playwright against a served build (playwright.config.ts:20, testDir './e2e'), not under Stryker's vitest runner (testRunner above). No mutant is ever exposed to it, no e2e assertion appears in any mutation score, and every mutation figure this repository reports excludes it entirely. Read no reassurance into its size. What it therefore does not buy. It catches defects large enough to change what a user sees: a crash, a control that stops responding, a value that fails to persist, an aria attribute that disappears. It does not catch the fine-grained branch and boundary flips mutation targets. Its assertions are deliberately tolerant of more than one correct behaviour, because that is what keeps an end-to-end test stable: e2e/integration/keyboard.spec.ts:173, 'Arrow Right from column 9 wraps or stops at edge', asserts only expect(selectedCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1) at line 199 and its own comment states that either wrapping or stopping passes, so a mutant flipping that edge comparison survives it, and the sibling edge tests at lines 202, 713 and 740 are written the same way. 55 of its integration-tier skips at main 414a7eb are runtime conditionals on fixture state, 23 of them test.skip(!emptyCell, ...), so a test can no-op on an unfavourable puzzle without failing. And it exercises whole flows, so an off-by-one in a branch the flow does not reach, an inverted guard on an error path, or a boundary reachable only from an unvisited state is invisible to it by construction. This is a residue, not a policy. The campaign's answer to the gap is extraction, not exclusion: logic worth measuring moves into src/lib and src/hooks where it is mutated, 18 files' worth since the residue was first counted, Board.tsx's cell-class and memo-comparator derivations among them. This note justifies only what _unmeasured_residue_files names, file by file, minus the two refusals recorded above. Applied as a category it would also retire Board.tsx, whose mutants are computation behind a short JSX tree, and it would stop being honest. Any file here later found to carry non-trivial logic belongs in extraction follow-up, not under this note.
_comment_thresholds: high/low are display thresholds (the portal reads them for its ok/warn coloring); 'break' is deliberately absent. A break threshold here was a second, independent gate at 90 while the real floors live in api/mutation-floors.json (hooks 100, surface 97), which is the two-sources problem. The enforcing gate is each scope's aggregate job in nightly-mutation.yml, which reads its floor from that file, and every shard step already runs continue-on-error because the aggregate is the scope's gate. Do not reintroduce break without deleting the aggregate gates.
_comment_dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Bounds one thing only: the single initial test run Stryker performs before any mutant is tested. It is not the mutation phase's budget; each mutant's own run is bounded separately by timeoutMS (5000 ms) and timeoutFactor (1.5), both left at their defaults, and it is those per-mutant limits, not this ceiling, that produce the Timeout kills. The value is measured, not assumed: across all 77 shards of hosted run 34928015321 the slowest initial test run took 90 seconds (median 84), and the same suite (2895 tests at local head f442807) measured locally at 4 minutes 08 seconds, or 8 minutes 28 under heavy concurrent load, so 20 minutes is roughly 13x the worst hosted shard and still 2.4x the most contended local measurement: a genuinely hung initial run fails in a third of an hour instead of two. It is deliberately unequal to both containing job timeouts in nightly-mutation.yml (surface 120, hooks 90): when the ceiling and a job timeout shared a number, a cancellation could not say which limit had fired.
